examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law
examples.worked_solution:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∧Q)∧(Q∨Q) & ≡(P∧Q)∧Q \\  & ≡P∧(Q∧Q) \\  & ≡P∧Q.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Simplify the following sentence: "$8$ is even and it is an even number, and $8$ is even and it is a positive number."
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we simplify the phrase "$8$ is even and it is an even number" to just "$8$ is even." The sentence now reads

"$8$ is even, and $8$ is even and it is a positive number."

Then, using the associative law, we can move the comma in the sentence:

"$8$ is even and $8$ is even, and it is a positive number."

Now, we simplify the phrase "$8$ is even and $8$ is even" to just "$8$ is even." The sentence now reads

"$8$ is even, and it is a positive number."

Finally, we simplify the sentence to

"$8$ is even and positive."
